correctness.rationale: For each m>=3, the directed edge vectors have norm squared 2 and Gram matrix with diag 2, off-diagonal -1 except +1 at the two links to the reversed edge. The quadratic block coefficients solve the Dirichlet second-difference equation exactly and sum to one by a verified cubic identity. Their Gram products equal lambda on every positively weighted unreversed vertex and lambda(m-1)/2 >= lambda at the flipped vertex, giving norm squared lambda and global optimality via an exact weighted squared-distance certificate. The same certificate proves uniqueness for any possible translated center. The flipped distance deficit is exactly lambda(m-3) and its equality boundary is m=3. Closed denominator and position extremality follow from a direct polynomial identity. Exact-rational exhaustive checks for 322 finite instances are corroborative only, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object full text classifies arbitrary directed path root polytopes as simplices, without Euclidean enclosing-ball measurements. The more general directed-root-polytope full text studies graph dissections and arithmetic, not minimum spheres. An all-vertex-sphere optimality criterion alone would not determine the optimizer when the all-vertex sphere is not minimal. The consistently oriented orientation, whose center and radius can be computed as in the proof, does not imply the formula after changing a sign. Indexed searches under quiver, type-A simple roots, incidence simplex, flip, circumradius, and Chebyshev-ball aliases returned no formula implying the present position-dependent radius and strict flipped-vertex screening.

value.rationale: A single arrow reversal is the smallest possible orientation defect of a canonical type-A directed root simplex. The result proves an all-dimensional qualitative instability of the minimum enclosing sphere: one specified vertex becomes strictly noncontact for every m>=4, so the enclosing sphere is completely controlled by the opposite facet. Its exact clearance and the sharp dependence on the reversal position (central versus endpoint defects) are not consequences of simplex combinatorics or the known all-vertex sphere criterion. This resolves the natural first nonmonotone orientation case with a full center, radius, contact and extremal-position classification, furnishing a structural test family for general root-polytope sphere problems.
